correctness.rationale: Exterior-neighbor counts are |T|−1_{i∈T} and |S|−1_{j∈S}. A one-sided triple is minimal. A mixed minimal fort cannot contain a triple; a singleton on one side would force the opposite side to include all indices except possibly the singleton's index, which for two or fewer opposing vertices leaves only n=3 and the complementary pair. Exterior vertices on the singleton side then see exactly one, so this case fails. In the 2+2 case exclusion of singleton exterior neighborhoods is equivalent to S=T. A fort disjoint from blue cannot be penetrated, and a nonempty terminal white set is a fort; excluding the classified forts gives the complete polynomial and minimum-set formula. Summing all triple inequalities gives the sharp fractional lower bound, and equality makes every triple tight; for n≥4 two common indices compare any two vertex weights in a side. The n=3 counterexample to uniqueness is feasible. Disjoint triple partitions, plus an aligned four-set when n≡2 mod 3, attain the rounded fractional bound. The submitted exact subset checker and recorded finite evidence were inspected, not executed.
